proof: THE WAGE AND SALARY SCHEDULE, PDF page 198 of the FY2015 annual town report: 20 GRADES against STEP 1 to STEP 8, in HOURLY RATES of pay -- not salaries and not an appropriation. THE COLUMNS ARE NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER, which reads `Grade | Step 1 | Step 2 | ... | Step 8` in white on black across the top of the grid. THE PAGE PRINTS NO TOTAL ANYWHERE and nothing on it adds to anything, so there is NO arithmetic to close. It is checked on the shape the grid asserts about itself, which is weaker than arithmetic and says so: a misread digit survives it untouched. What is declared is that EVERY ONE OF THE 20 ROWS CARRIES EXACTLY 8 FIGURES -- the printed header says how wide a row is, and a row that came out seven cells long is a rate lost -- and that the GRADE never goes backwards through all 160 cells. 160 of 160 cells are transcribed, with no cell blank anywhere on the grid. A REGULARITY WAS TESTED AND REFUSED AS A CHECK. The steps sit about 3% apart and it is tempting to use that as the arithmetic the page lacks; `round(step_1 x 1.03^(n-1))` does not reproduce the grid, so publishing it would be a hypothesis dressed as a proof. The same test failed on FY2022's schedule for the same reason. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: what anybody was paid. A rate table is a schedule of rates, not a payroll -- it says nothing about hours, headcount, which grade any post sits in, or which fund pays it. The job titles and their grades are printed as PROSE on this same page and are not transcribed here.
